title: Types of routes - 4.0
synopsis: OpenSIPS routing logic uses several types of routes. Each type of route is triggered by a certain event and allows you to process a certain type of message (request or reply).

route_types.name: route
route_types.description: Request routing block. It contains a set of actions to be taken for SIP requests.
route_types.trigger_condition: receiving an external request from the network.

route_types.name: branch_route
route_types.description: Request's branch routing block. It contains a set of actions to be taken for each branch of a SIP request.
route_types.trigger_condition: preparation a new branch (of a request); the branch is well formed, but not yet sent out.

route_types.name: failure_route
route_types.description: Failed transaction routing block. It contains a set of actions to be taken each transaction that received only negative replies (>=300) for all branches.
route_types.trigger_condition: receiving or generation(internal) of a negative reply that completes the transaction (all branches are terminated with negative replies)

route_types.name: onreply_route
route_types.description: Reply routing block. It contains a set of actions to be taken for SIP replies.
route_types.trigger_condition: receiving of a reply from the network

route_types.name: error_route
route_types.description: The error route is executed automatically when a parsing error occurs during SIP request processing, or when a script assert fails. It allows the administrator to decide what to do in such error cases.

route_types.name: local_route
route_types.description: The local route is executed automatically when a new SIP request is generated by TM, internally (no UAC side). This is a route intended to be used for message inspection, accounting and for applying last changes on the message headers. Routing and signaling functions are not allowed.
route_types.trigger_condition: TM generating a brand new request

route_types.name: startup_route
route_types.description: The startup_route is executed only once when OpenSIPS is started and before the processing of SIP messages begins. This is useful if some initiation actions are needed, like loading some data in the cache, to ease up the future processing. Notice that this route, compared to the others is not triggered at the receipt of a message, so the functions that can be called here must not do processing on the message.
route_types.trigger_condition: At startup, before the listener processes are started.

route_types.name: timer_route
route_types.description: The timer_route is a route executed periodically at a configured interval of time specified next to the name (in seconds). Similar to startup_route, this route does not process a SIP message. Multiple timer routes (possibly at differing running intervals) are allowed.

route_types.name: event_route
route_types.description: The event_route is used by the OpenSIPS Event Interface to execute script code when an event is triggered. The name of the route is the event that has to be handled by that route. The route itself is executed asynchronously with regards to the trigger moment.
route_types.trigger_condition: the event_route module when an event raised by the OpenSIPS Event Interface
